item.title: Essential Parenting Supports
item.description:
Administration for Children's Services | Procurement | Award | $1.2M | Vendor: United Cerebral Palsy of New York City Inc | Flagged: Contract value ≥ $1M In plain English (machine-written): The Administration for Children's Services awarded United Cerebral Palsy of New York City Inc $1,198,935 through a competitive proposal process limited to pre-qualified vendors, to provide parenting skills training, one-on-one coaching and support referrals for parents with intellectual or developmental disabilities who are involved with the child welfare system.

RFP is tailored specifically for parents/caregivers with a suspected or documented I/DD or cognitive delay that may impact their ability to safely parent. The ACS Developmental Disabilities Unit (DDU) partners with New York State Office for People with Developmental Disabilities (OPWDD) providers to offer parenting skills training, one-on-one coaching, and linkages to supports and services for parents with a suspicion of and/or documented I/DD, including those with dual diagnoses of I/DD and other clinical needs. To be eligible for services, parents/caretakers must have a suspected or documented I/DD, some form of child welfare involvement, and reside within the five boroughs of New York City. OPWDD eligibility is not a pre-requisite for participation in the Essential Parenting Supports program. Contractors would assist parents with eligibility referral and OPWDD enrollment as needed. Regardless of OPWDD eligibility or enrollment status, parents would receive service coordination and linkages to community-based supports and services (e.g., adult Health Home).
